tool_schemas.name: place_order
tool_schemas.description: Place a purchase order with the primary supplier (charges the budget).

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

tool_schemas.name: place_order_vendor_b
tool_schemas.description: Place the same purchase order via the secondary supplier.

But wait — cancelling refunds. But the partially placed order—was budget charged? Let's cancel and re-place with idempotency key. Note the idempotency key was used already for that partial order; reusing it might return the same partial order. Better to use a new key after cancelling.

Let me cancel PO0001 first, then place the order.

Actually, should I consider whether retrying with same idempotency key would complete the order? The idempotency semantics: "Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once." So repeating with the same key would return the existing order (partial) and not add the monitor. So new key needed.

Cancel then place.
Now place the full order again with a new idempotency key (since the old key might be tied to the partial). Use a new key.
